body: Quantum Fund (with Jim Rogers from 1973) compounded roughly ~30% a year from 1969 to 2000 by commonly cited estimates (unaudited, press figures). Structural edge: global macro mandate, leverage, and later Druckenmiller as PM. Process edge: reflexivity - market prices do not just reflect fundamentals, they change them (rising stock prices let firms raise cheap capital, rising collateral values let banks lend more), producing self-reinforcing booms that overshoot and then reverse. He looks for a prevailing bias plus a flaw, invests early in the boom, and shorts when the trend is exhausted; 'invest first, investigate later' with small size, then add. Signature trade: 1992 sterling short with Druckenmiller (~$1bn widely reported; ~$1.8bn for the week per Wikipedia). Mistakes: Oct 1987 he was positioned for a Japan crash and lost heavily selling US futures near the low (~$300m+ in days, figure unverified); 1998 Russia losses (~$2bn, unverified); 2000 tech losses. Copyable: map credit-fuelled feedback loops (India 2007 infra/realty, 2023-24 PSU rerating, 2024 SME IPOs) and ask what breaks the loop (funding, regulation, supply); scale in as evidence confirms. Not copyable: macro leverage and access.

data.copyable: identify loops and their break points
data.edge_process: reflexive feedback loops, bias + flaw, probe then scale

title: George Soros - reflexivity and boom-bust trading
